pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Update window.rs PresentMode docs to clarify which PresentMode will panic and which will fallback
pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes contradictory docs in Window::PresentMode partaining to PresentMode fallback behavior. Fix based on commit history showing the most recent update didn't remove old references to the gracefal fallback for Immediate and Mailbox.
- Fixes #5831 

## Solution

- Updated the docs for Window::PresentMode itself and for each individual enum variant to clarify which will fallback and which will panic.

issue_context.title: `bevy_window::PresentMode` says `Immediate` and `Mailbox` will panic if unsupported, but also says they will fallback to `Fifo` if unsupported
issue_context.body:
Hi! I was browsing Bevy's documentation, just thinking up ideas for games, when I chanced upon some rather curious documentation.

Within [`bevy_window::PresentMode`](https://docs.rs/bevy_window/0.8.1/bevy_window/enum.PresentMode.html)'s documentation, it states the following:

> `Immediate` or `Mailbox` will gracefully fallback to `Fifo` when unavailable.

This statement is also repeated in the [descriptions of `Immediate`](https://docs.rs/bevy_window/0.8.1/bevy_window/enum.PresentMode.html#variant.Immediate) and [`Mailbox`](https://docs.rs/bevy_window/0.8.1/bevy_window/enum.PresentMode.html#variant.Mailbox):

> Will fallback to `Fifo` if unavailable on the selected platform and backend.

However, under both variants, there's also this statement which seems to conflict with the above statements:

> Selecting this variant will panic if not supported, it is preferred to use `PresentMode::AutoNoVsync`.

Having read all this, I'm now confused as to whether `Immediate` and `Mailbox` are safe to use because they will fall back to `Fifo` if they're unsupported, or if I should prefer another mode due to the possibility of a panic.

To be clear: I will most likely never need to use `PresentMode` myself, so whatever is meant here will not mean much to me. But I fear that the documentation may be confusing to others, so I hope it can be updated to avoid this conflict of statements.
comments: If I remember correctly, the gracious fallback behavior is not true anymore and should be removed. Now only the ˋAutoˋ variants do fallback
Hi is this just a docs update? I would be happy to update it and submit a PR

review_comments:
Hey, thanks for fixing the documentation. :)

Anyways, I figured I should point out an error I noticed. These doc-comments don't seem to be respecting the 80-character-per-line max that the rest of the doc-comments are following. It's not a huge deal that it doesn't follow the standard set by other doc-comments, it'd just be nice if everything was consistent.

This would need to be fixed in another PR (or in a commit by a member) since this PR is already merged, but I thought it was worth pointing out.
Hey thanks for pointing it out! It's my first time doing such a thing so didn't realize that was important. Unless it's fixed otherwise I'll submit another PR to correct it. My apologies!

Ah, no need to apologize, or even worry about it. Being a code style issue (and also because it doesn't affect how documentation is generated), I consider it pretty minor in the grand scheme of things. :)
doc style is not strictly enforced, and not consistent through the codebase. Personally I most of the time try to stick to under 100 characters. Sometimes 120...
Good to know anyways! I'll try and be more mindful of the quality and consistency in the future, thank you guys!
